title: An organization records the AWS account it provisions into
description:
**Phase 1 of 5.**

- **Blocked by:** nothing
- **Runs in parallel with:** the assume-role story
- **Unblocks:** the computer launch story, and the ceiling story in the spend epic

---
The organization record grows a home: which AWS account, which role, which ExternalId, and which of the two setup paths it came through.

Path A is an account the customer already owns and pays for. Path B is an account Anthus created and re-bills, delivered by hand and priced accordingly. The record has to distinguish them, because they carry different obligations and Path B carries credit risk.

An organization with no AWS account recorded is not broken — it is one that has paid but not yet been provisioned, which is a real and expected state between checkout and enablement.

**Done when:** the scenarios exist and fail for the right reason.

comments.author: unknown
comments.text:
Feature: Cross-account provisioning

  Scenario: A provisioned organization knows its AWS home
    Given an organization that has completed provisioning
    Then it records the customer AWS account id
    And it records the cross-account role
    And it records whether the account is customer-owned or Anthus-managed

  Scenario: A paid organization awaiting provisioning has no AWS home yet
    Given an organization that has paid but not been provisioned
    Then it records no customer AWS account
    And its status is pending

comments.author: home
comments.text: On develop: organization records `aws_account_id`, `aws_cross_account_role`, `aws_external_id`, `aws_setup_path` (`org_records.provision_organization_aws`). Covered by `features/cross_account_provisioning.feature` (provisioned home / paid-but-unprovisioned). Board was behind the kernel.
